head: 3514ccf0a6a172528a33691dcc1bca9d14cdf15d
classification_reasons: Spec is now tight: both of spec.md's Flagged concerns are closed with concrete, panel-recorded decisions (empty input raises ValueError('mean() requires at least one value') from a guard clause mean owns; parameter type is Sequence[float]), and plan.md carries the exact signature and body, so acceptance for every case (normal, single-element, empty) is a single measurable assertion.

Blast radius is small: the diff touches only changes/0002-add-mean-helper-to-sample-pkg/{spec.md,plan.md,status.yaml,evidence/**} in phase (b) itself; the code files plan.md names for phase (c) (sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py, tests/test_calc.py) are not yet touched, are not on sdlc.yaml's risk_list, and are not guardrail files.

Coverage is the criterion that keeps this non-routine: mean is a brand-new function with no existing test exercising it today; the three tests that will cover it (test_mean, test_mean_single_element, test_mean_empty) are written in the same change, not pre-existing, so 'code the existing tests already cover' does not hold. Per the article/build-guide bar, all three routine conditions must hold, and this one does not.
attempted: Intent: re-checked intent.md's Proposed outcome bullet 5 (spec closes flagged concerns as 'decided (by panel): ...', PR opens with 'Decisions taken for you (N)', evidence/ carries decisions-b.md and panel/ files) against the current diff. All three now exist: decisions-b.json/.md, evidence/panel/b-1-*, b-2-*, b-items.json, and both spec.md Flagged concerns bullets literally begin with 'decided (by panel): ...'. The gap that caused the prior escalate (at HEAD 9c501fb) is closed.

Spec and plan: read spec.md Requirements/Design/Open questions/Flagged concerns/Acceptance and plan.md Files/Order/Risks/Options/Proof end to end. Both flagged concerns are closed with matching, concrete decisions (Sequence[float]; explicit ValueError guard), plan.md's step 1 code block matches both decisions exactly, and plan.md's Options-not-taken section correctly attributes the rejected ZeroDivisionError-propagation and Iterable[float]/Collection[float] alternatives to the panel round. One cosmetic defect found and judged non-blocking: spec.md's Flagged concerns bullets retain the original 'is undecided: ...' concern text appended after the 'decided (by panel): ...' prefix (and concern 2's prefix is duplicated: 'decided (by panel): decided (by panel): ...'), a mechanical text-splice artifact from how the decision string was inserted. It is confusing to read in isolation but is not the document a build-phase implementer would actually build from (plan.md is unambiguous and internally consistent), it changes no behavior, leaks no data, and breaches no policy, so per REVIEW.md's 'What Important means here' it is a nit, not an escalate reason.

Proof: compared decisions-b.json/.md and evidence/panel/b-1-*, b-2-* (reviewer, devil's advocate, conciliator, one round each) against sample_pkg/calc.py's actual current code. The panel's factual claims check out against the real file: divide raises ZeroDivisionError('b must not be zero') and percent is literally divide(part * 100, whole), so the reviewer's 'percent precedent' argument and the advocate's rebuttal are both grounded in the real codebase, not invented. evidence/panel/b-items.json still shows 'decided: 0' and all three items 'pending' even though decisions-b.json records two decisions; this is a stale bookkeeping snapshot (items.json appears to predate the decisions being applied) rather than a sign the decisions weren't actually made — decisions-b.json, decisions-b.md and the updated spec.md/plan.md text all agree with each other on what was decided.

Blast radius: diff-b.patch's --stat header lists only files under changes/0002-add-mean-helper-to-sample-pkg/ (spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml, evidence/**); no sample_pkg/*.py, tests/*.py, .claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md or sdlc.yaml is touched. None of sdlc.yaml's risk_list items (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) apply. Confirmed by reading sdlc.yaml directly.

Policies: re-read spec.md's per-skill applicability calls (security-baseline, ux-conventions, data-conventions all correctly n/a for a pure in-process arithmetic helper; coding-standards rule 2's 'match the surrounding code' and rule 5's 'no unnecessary dependency' are the rules the panel actually leaned on for both decisions) — reasoning is honest and specific to this codebase, not generic boilerplate.

Tests: no test files are touched in this phase-(b) diff, consistent with design-only scope; plan.md's Proof section names the three tests to be added in phase (c) and pins test_mean_empty to `pytest.raises(ValueError)` around `mean([])`, which pins mean's own guard clause rather than a coincidental ZeroDivisionError from divide — the devil's advocate's own point in evidence/panel/b-1-advocate.md ('the test would pass with the bug still in' under the rejected option) is exactly what this decision avoids.

Guardrail check: confirmed no diff hunk touches .claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md or sdlc.yaml; status.yaml's own review_override: deferred field is unchanged by this diff (only phase, iterations and updated_at moved), consistent with a run that is not allowed to edit that guardrail-adjacent per-change config beyond its own bookkeeping fields.
